title: Slowly down the continent
text: The grand tour took months because transport gave no {{1}}: you rode, you sailed, you waited for the wind. What began as necessity is now a {{2}} of intention. Slow travel — journeys chosen for the travelling rather than despite it — has moved from fringe to {{3}}, fuelled by travellers who would rather read the landscape than {{4}} over it at ten kilometres. The logic is partly carbon arithmetic, but its {{5}} is older: the journey is not dead time between destinations but the {{6}} part of the trip. Slow converts cite the {{7}} that only come from ground level: borders you feel, languages that change at the pace of dialect rather than flight, meals in towns you would never have {{8}} at 30,000 feet. The travel industry, ever alert, now sells slowness at a premium — which raises the obvious irony, that the richest form of travel has become the one our great-grandparents could least afford.

gaps.explanation: 'transport gave no alternative' — no other choice; altercation = a heated argument.
'now a statement of intention' — a deliberate declaration; stipend = a fixed payment.
'from fringe to mainstream' — from the edges to the centre; mainstay = the person or thing a group depends on.
'rather than skim over it' — glide over the surface without engaging; skid = slide out of control.
'its philosophy is older' — its underlying way of thinking; physiology = the science of the body, philology = historical linguistics.
'but the substance of the trip' — the real content, as opposed to dead time; subtext = an underlying meaning.
'cite the pleasures that only come from ground level' — the enjoyments; leisure = free time as a mass noun.
'towns you would never have spotted at 30,000 feet' — caught sight of; squander = waste.
